info.title: ZoneFlow local API
info.summary: REST API of the ZoneFlow standalone firmware.
info.description: Served by the controller on the local network. Not tested on hardware yet: the firmware has run only in host unit tests. Every route is checked against the firmware route table by `test/host/web_openapi_test.cpp`.

get.description: Whether an admin password exists and whether this request carries a valid session. For a cookie session it also returns the CSRF token, so a reloaded page can recover it.

post.description: Rate limited per client address (5 free failures, then 1 s doubling to 15 min) and in total (30 failures in 5 min lock everyone out for 60 s). A refused attempt answers 429 with Retry-After.

200.description: Logged in. Also sets the `zf_session` cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict).

post.description: Only while no password exists. The setup code is shown on the device display and serial log, never over the network; knowing it proves physical access. Rate limited like login.
Ends this session and clears the cookie.

200.description: Changed. Every other session is signed out; this is the new one.

put.description: Partial update. Turning HTTPS on or off takes effect after a reboot (`restart_required`).

get.description: Everything a dashboard needs in one call: zones, master, queue, sensors, rain delay, inhibits, faults, network and OTA state.

On connect the server sends a `state` message (same body as GET /status), then one message per change: `event` for each controller event, `state` when the snapshot changed (at most every 500 ms, and at least every 30 s), `network` and `ota` when those change, and a comment line every 15 s as keep-alive. At most 3 streams are open at once; a fourth gets 503.

200.description: An endless `text/event-stream`. See the API reference page for the event names and payloads.

parameters.name: zone
parameters.description: Zone number as printed on the terminal block, 1 to zone_count.

patch.description: Changes the zone's entry in the configuration. Validation errors name the field in `error.path`.

parameters.description: Zone number as printed on the terminal block, 1 to zone_count.

post.summary: Run a zone for N seconds
post.description: Adds a manual run to the end of the queue. The zone driver clamps the time to the zone's `max_run_s` (the answer shows the clamped value). Refused (409) for a disabled zone (zone_disabled), a locked-out zone (locked_out), a resting zone (zone_resting, with Retry-After), a locked-out master (master_locked_out), without 24 VAC and during maintenance (inhibited). The answer waits up to 250 ms for the control task: a rejection comes back as an error (see RunRejection), an accepted command as 202 with confirmed true. If no verdict arrives in time the answer is 202 with confirmed false and a rejection, if any, appears on the event stream as command_rejected.

post.description: Closes the zone if it is the running queue entry (the queue then moves on). A zone that is only queued further back gives 409 `not_head`; use POST /queue/stop.

post.description: A fault whose cause is still present is raised again on the next sample. Output-stage faults are acknowledged as well, except a keep-alive detector fault (faults.hardware.repair_needed), which needs POST /faults/acknowledge-repair. Trip counts are reset.

202.description: Command queued for the control task

post.summary: Confirm that the board was repaired after a keep-alive detector fault
post.description: A fault of a safety layer (hardware design 19.7 steps 1, 2, 2b, 5b and 9: keepalive_detector, keepalive_bridged, relay_gate_bleed; and since the hardware answers to section 19 the rectifier fault of 19.10, rectifier_fault, the over-voltage of rule 18, supply_over_voltage, and a held set input of the latch of 19.8, latch_input_held) means the board needs repair, so it is not cleared with one press. This is the second, deliberate action: the body must say repaired: true. 409 `no_repair_fault` when no such fault is active. The board then learns its detector release times again, and the full self-test runs before any valve opens.

202.description: Command queued for the control task

put.description: Validated as a whole; nothing changes on error and `error.path` names the field. Missing fields take defaults, unknown fields are ignored. Nested deeper than 16 levels is rejected before parsing. A document from newer firmware is refused (400, error.code unsupported_schema, error.path schema, the core's message).

get.description: The configuration with a small header. Never contains secrets: no WiFi credentials, password hash, sessions, setup code or TLS key.

requestBody.description: A backup file from GET /config/backup, or a bare configuration document.

post.description: A document from newer firmware is refused (400, error.code unsupported_schema, error.path schema, the core's message).

put.summary: Set the clock or the time zone
put.description: `utc` sets the clock (and the RTC) by hand; SNTP overrides it at the next sync. `timezone` is a POSIX TZ string stored in the configuration.

post.description: The stored WiFi credentials stay until new ones connect; after 15 minutes without a new setup the device returns to the stored network. Same as the long-press on the device.

get.description: Used by the setup page on the SoftAP. Never returns the setup code.

Only while SoftAP provisioning runs (409 `not_provisioning` otherwise), and only from a client joined to the setup access point (403 `setup_ap_only` from the home network, which the station joins before provisioning ends). The setup code is the WPA2 passphrase of that access point, so a client on it has already proven it knows the code.

post.description: Only while SoftAP provisioning runs, and only from a client joined to the setup access point (403 `setup_ap_only` otherwise). Optionally sets the first admin password.

202.description: Handed to the provisioning manager; poll GET /provision

post.description: Outputs are forced off by the restart handler.
Stops watering, then erases configuration, runtime state, WiFi credentials, the admin password, sessions, web settings and the TLS certificate. The setup code is kept so a printed label stays valid.

Refused (409 `zones_active`) while a zone runs unless `force=true`. Before writing, the controller is put in maintenance mode, which closes every valve and blocks starts. The header is checked (ESP32-S3, project `zoneflow-fw`) before anything is written; the image is verified at the end. The new image must confirm itself after boot, otherwise the bootloader rolls back.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Update even while watering (outputs are still forced off first).

requestBody.description: The raw application image (`zoneflow-fw.bin` from a release).

202.description: Verified and set as boot image; the device restarts

post.summary: Download and install an image from a URL
post.description: HTTPS only, checked against the ESP-IDF certificate bundle; redirects are followed (GitHub release assets redirect to a CDN). Same safety rules as upload.

202.description: Download started; follow GET /firmware or the `ota` stream event

post.description: Replaces the web UI files. Does not touch the firmware or settings.

requestBody.description: A LittleFS image of the `www` partition (`www.bin` from a release).

202.description: Written; the UI is served from it at once

get.description: The `mqtt` object of the configuration, whether a password and a custom CA certificate are stored (never their values), and the client's connection state. Topic tree and Home Assistant discovery: [MQTT guide](https://syntroniks.github.io/zoneflow/firmware/mqtt/).

put.description: Partial update. Connection fields are validated by the core configuration (errors carry the field as `path`) and stored in the configuration; `password` and `ca_cert` are write-only and stored in NVS, outside the configuration and its backup. The client reconnects with the new settings within a second.

get.description: Runs (zone, source, planned and actual duration, end reason, current, volume), skipped and missed starts, faults, and system events (boot with reset reason, clock, configuration, rain delay, sensors, updates), newest first. Kept in flash in a ring of 1200 records; written in batches (within 60 s, faults at once). Page back with `before`; fetch new records with `after`. No secrets are recorded.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only records with a smaller id.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only records with a larger id.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only records at or after this time (Unix seconds).

put.description: Stores `setup_complete` (shown by GET /auth) in the web settings, outside the configuration and its backup. A factory reset clears it.

bearerAuth.description: Token from POST /auth/login. Scripts use this; no CSRF header needed.

cookieAuth.name: zf_session
cookieAuth.description: Set by login. Writes with the cookie also need the X-CSRF-Token header.

path.description: JSON path of the offending field, when there is one.

confirmed.description: Run commands only. true: the control task handled the command and did not reject it. false: no verdict within 250 ms; a rejection, if any, arrives on the event stream as command_rejected.

csrf.description: Only for a valid cookie session.

setup_complete.description: The web UI’s first-run steps were finished or skipped (PUT /setup). A hint for clients; it gates nothing.

token.description: Bearer token; the same value is in the cookie.

csrf.description: Send as X-CSRF-Token on writes that use the cookie.

tls_fingerprint_sha256.description: Of the self-signed certificate; empty if none.

protect_reads.description: GET routes need a session too.

https.description: Serve on port 443 with a self-signed certificate.

check_host.description: Refuse requests whose Host is not this device.

heap.description: free, min_free and largest_block cover all 8-bit heap, PSRAM included; internal_* cover internal RAM only.

locked_out.description: Latched fault on this zone; runs are refused until faults are cleared.

resting.description: The zone reached its maximum run time (summed across back-to-back runs) and must stay closed for driver.min_rest_s (spec section 2, rule 4).

rest_remaining_s.description: Seconds of rest left; 0 when not resting.

default_run_s.description: Duration of a run started without one (Home Assistant valve open, MQTT run with an empty payload). Clamped like any run.

learned_current_ma.description: Mean current measured with this zone open alone (master share removed), since the last restart; null until it has run alone. Basis for setting current_min_ma and current_max_ma.

default_run_s.description: Duration of a run started without one (Home Assistant valve open, MQTT run with an empty payload). Clamped like any run.

anchor.description: First day of an interval rule (local).

durations_s.description: Seconds per zone; index 0 is zone 1. 0 leaves the zone out.

obey_sensor.description: Skip while the rain sensor is active.

ProgramInput.description: Same as Program. `id` is optional on create and must match the path on replace.

pause_timeout_min.description: schedule.pause_timeout_min: a queue paused this long is stopped (event pause_expired).

paused_s.description: Seconds since the first pause while paused, else 0.

stop_in_s.description: While paused: seconds until the queue is stopped (pause_timeout_min after the first pause). Null otherwise.

RainDelayRequest.description: Exactly one of the two fields.

until_utc.description: Unix seconds, within the next 30 days.

current_sense_available.description: False while the valve-current readings are missing (fault current_sense_unavailable). Zones still run; open and short detection is blind.

over_current_tripped.description: The hardware over-current latch removed gate drive and released the relay (fault over_current_trip, latched until faults are cleared). The controller clears the latch itself by holding the keep-alive low for 1.5 s; the output switched on within 500 ms before is blamed, and after three trips in a day it stays off until faults are cleared.

sensor_supply_fault.description: The 5 V sensor supply switch reports over-current or over-temperature (fault sensor_supply). Read from the I/O expander during runs and every 10 minutes between them. Sent by firmware with the rev A output stage; optional in this schema so that older firmware and the web UI's mock controller still validate.

hardware.description: The output stage's latched self-test failure (hardware design 19.7), or null. While it is set nothing runs. repair_needed: one of the layers can no longer be relied on (steps 1, 2, 2b, 5b or 9); POST /faults/clear leaves it, POST /faults/acknowledge-repair clears it, and the board then learns its detector release times again. Sent by firmware with the rev A output stage; optional in this schema so that older firmware and the web UI's mock controller still validate.

step.description: Self-test step of the check, hardware design 19.7: "1", "2", "2b", "3", "4a", "4b", "4c", "5", "5b", "6", "7", "8" or "9". null for a check that is not a step of the sequence (bus error, the over-current latch of 19.8, a firmware limit, rule 16). A string since review A2 added steps 2b and 5b.

locked_out.description: Locked out after master.fault_lockout_count consecutive current faults on the master; every zone is blocked until faults are cleared.

fault_count.description: Consecutive current faults attributed to the master.

hardware.description: An output-stage fault blocks every start until acknowledged. Sent by firmware with the rev A output stage; optional in this schema so that older firmware and the web UI's mock controller still validate.

Config.description: The configuration document as stored and returned (every field present). The configuration document described in the firmware architecture, section 6. Missing fields take defaults; unknown fields are ignored. A document whose schema is newer than the firmware is refused with error.code unsupported_schema and path schema.

schema.description: Documents with schema 1 are accepted and migrated (adds `mqtt` and `zones[].default_run_s`).

zones.description: Always 8 entries; zones above zone_count are kept but not used.

local.description: Local wall-clock time, ISO 8601 without offset.

password.description: Empty or absent for an open network; else 8 to 64.

admin_password.description: Sets the first admin password if none exists.

RunRejection.description: Error answer of a run command. error.code is the controller's RunError: invalid_zone, unknown_program, zero_duration, queue_full, already_queued, inhibited, nothing_to_run, locked_out, zone_resting, master_locked_out, hardware_fault (or inhibited when maintenance or missing 24 VAC is known beforehand). zone_resting answers carry Retry-After with the seconds of rest left.

MqttSettings.description: The `mqtt` object of the configuration document (schema 2).

host.description: Broker host name or IP address, without scheme or port. Required when enabled.

ca.description: With TLS: verify the broker against the ESP-IDF certificate bundle (public CAs) or against the CA certificate stored with `ca_cert`.

base_topic.description: Root of every topic. Empty: `zoneflow/<device id>`. No wildcards, no leading or trailing `/`.

ha_zone_entity.description: Home Assistant entity type for zones.

reconnect_attempt.description: Attempts since the last successful connection.

commands_rejected.description: Invalid, retained, rate-limited or refused by the controller.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` for the next older page; null when there is none.

oldest_id.description: Oldest id still kept (approximately: a damaged chunk inside the range is skipped).

capacity.description: Records the log holds at most; older ones are overwritten.

unsaved.description: Records not yet written to flash (lost on a power cut; written within 60 s, faults at once).

Hardware.description: The rev A output stage (I/O expander, valve-common relay, two keep-alive detectors) and the current measurement. Hardware design section 19. Nothing here has been measured on a board. Sent by firmware with the rev A output stage; optional in this schema so that older firmware and the web UI's mock controller still validate.

phase.description: none: a board without a sequenced stage. ready: the relay is closed and valves may switch. starting and stopping: the self-test before and after a run. polling: the 10-minute check between runs.

zones_fitted.description: From the board's variant strap, read in the start-up self-test; null before.

check.description: The latched failed check, or null.

step.description: Self-test step of the check (19.7): "1" to "9" with "2b", "4a" to "4c" and "5b". null when no check is latched, or for a check that is not a step (bus error, the over-current latch of 19.8, a firmware limit, rule 16).

detectors.description: Last measured detector times, ms (0 = not measured), and this board's stored release times. Pass limits (hardware design 19.7 since the hardware answers to section 19): enable within 150 ms; release 150 to 1000 ms (drive) and 50 to 1600 ms (relay), and each within 0.40 to 1.70 times the stored value once the board is commissioned.

commissioned.description: The board has stored release times. false: step 9 applies its absolute limits only, and not_commissioned is active.

reference_drive_ms.description: Stored release time of the gate-drive detector, the median of five stop tests at commissioning; null when not commissioned.

reference_relay_ms.description: Stored release time of the relay detector; null when not commissioned.

waiting_for_temperature.description: Not commissioned, and the ESP32-S3 die temperature is outside 25 to 50 C or unknown: commissioning waits and is tried again every 10 minutes (hardware design 19.7, Commissioning, item 2).

mains_hz.description: From the zero-cross signal; null when unknown.

channel.description: Amplifier channel of the latest window: low when the high-gain channel clipped.

noise_floor_ma.description: Learned with the relay open; removed in quadrature.

dc_ma.description: Mean shift of the latest window against the idle mean: a DC component (fault zone_dc_current).

last_trip_ma.description: Current window before the last over-current trip.

supply.description: Hardware design 19.10: window means, mV, null until read. vin_mon_mv is VIN_MON (the rectified supply divided by 31): step 0 needs 0.60 to 1.50 V; under 0.60 V supply_low, above 1.50 V supply_high, under 0.10 V with mains present for 2 s rectifier_fault. rest_lo_mv and rest_hi_mv are the current channels at rest: limits 700 to 880 mV and 680 to 900 mV; both above 900 mV is supply_over_voltage (rule 18), one outside its limits a lost current measurement (rule 19).

current_lost.description: Hardware design rule 19: why the current measurement counts as lost. Anything but none skips steps 5, 5b and 6 and rule 6, zones still run, and current_sense_unavailable is active for as long as it lasts.

checks_skipped.description: Starts since boot that skipped steps 5, 5b and 6 for lack of current readings (rule 19).

idle_trips.description: Over-current trips with no valve bit low since boot (hardware design 19.8): not counted against an output; a second one in a row is latch_input_held.

repaired.description: The person states the board was repaired.

BadRequest.description: Invalid body or parameter; `error.path` names the field

Unauthorized.description: No valid session (`unauthorized`), or no admin password yet (`password_not_set`)

Forbidden.description: Host not this device (`bad_host`), cross-origin write (`bad_origin`), missing CSRF header (`csrf`), or a provisioning route from outside the setup access point (`setup_ap_only`)

NotFound.description: No such zone, program or route

Conflict.description: Refused in the current state (zone disabled, inhibited, update running, ...)

TooLarge.description: Body larger than the route allows (checked before reading)

TooManyRequests.description: Too many failed attempts; see Retry-After
